messages:
jordan: Heads-up — planning a rolling reboot + node drains for the apac-saturn GPU pool tonight 23:00-01:00 UTC. Targeting NIC microcode + driver update to fix intermittent microburst backpressure we've seen at high concurrency. Will do canary -> gradual roll.
liya: How many GPUs/nodes will be touched? any customer-facing quota changes?
jordan: Rough numbers: ~120 GPUs across 6 racks (az9/az10). Canary will be 2 racks (~40 GPUs). No quota changes planned, but we'll temporarily reduce burst capacity and pause preemptible placement for low-tier jobs during the window.
marc: Suggest we reserve 20% buffer in eu/us pools to absorb traffic, and enable routing-policy to prefer eu for latency-tolerant jobs. Also recommend prewarming KV cache on canary after drain.
sree: Ops checklist draft: 1) create maintenance ticket 2) run canary on 2 racks 3) validate p99 token latency and model error rates 4) warm kv-prefix cache and sampled keyspace 5) roll 1 rack at a time, wait 10m post-warm for metrics.
ops-bot: Maintenance ticket created: INF-6721 — scheduled 2026-03-21 23:00-01:00 UTC. Canary: racks saturn-rack-03/04.
emily: Small reminder: APAC support window overlaps with midnight local — I'll be on-call. If we see any elevation in 5xx, start rollback immediately and switch routing to eu/us fallback.
liya: Can we include the exact drain commands in the runbook so on-call doesn't need to improvise?
jordan: Yep. Runbook snippet (use cordon + drain with grace):
```bash
kubectl cordon gpu-node-xx
kubectl drain gpu-node-xx --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120 --force
# after patch, uncordon
kubectl uncordon gpu-node-xx
```
marc: For model-serving (long KV cache warm), do a lightweight kv-seed before routing full traffic:
```bash
# sample traffic to warm prefix cache
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_TOKEN" -d '{"input":"seed prompt"}' https://host/api/v1/generate --rate 10/s --duration 2m
```
sree: Metrics to watch: per-node GPU utilization, host NIC tx/rx queue drops, p50/p95/p99 token latency, model error rate, request queuing depth. We'll create a Grafana dashboard and an alertset scoped to the canary racks.
liya: Cost note — if canary goes long and we keep buffer in eu/us, that increases cross-region egress cost. Can we limit fallback percentage to 15% to keep costs bounded?
marc: Agreed. Set fallback routing cap to 15% and enable cost-tagging on any fallback requests. Finance is OK with a small spike but asked to avoid open-ended re-routes.
emily: Rollback plan: stop rollout, re-image nodes (if necessary), move canary traffic back to pre-rollover snapshots, unpatch NIC driver. Ops will communicate outage window to any impacted Dedicated customers if SLA thresholds are hit.
jordan: Communication plan: post in #customer-comm 2 hours before with high-level note, update status page if we hit any degraded signals. I'll update the runbook and add links to ticket/graphs.
ops-bot: Canary deployment started (saturn-rack-03). Monitoring hooks: infra-grafana/canary-saturn-03, tracer/kv-warm.
liya: Thanks — I'll be watching the grafana panels and will confirm go/no-go after the 20m warm window. :thumbsup:
marc: I'll tweak routing-policy and cost tags now so they're ready.
sree: All set from my side, on-call rotation updated. If anything odd, @jordan and @emily please escalate immediately.
jordan: Great — thanks team. Will post a short update at +30m and after full roll.
